title: Weakly associated primes contract along a finite ring map
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $S$ is generated by finitely many elements as an $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let $P$ be any $S$-module, regarded as an $R$-module by $r x=\varphi(r)x$. For a commutative ring $T$ and a $T$-module $N$, let $\operatorname{WeakAss}_T(N)$ be the set of prime ideals minimal among the prime ideals containing $\operatorname{Ann}_T(x)=\{t\in T:tx=0\}$ for some $x\in N$. If $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_S(P)$, then $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_R(P)$. There is no Noetherian hypothesis on the rings and no finite-generation hypothesis on $P$.

source.place: Tag 05E1, lemma-weakly-ass-finite-ring-map, inclusion from the image of WeakAss_S(P) to WeakAss_R(P); equivalently the finite-pushforward ingredient Tag 05EZ in divisors.tex. https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05E1

proof.text: Choose $m\in P$ such that $\mathfrak q$ is minimal over $J=\operatorname{Ann}_S(m)$, and put $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Then $J\subseteq\mathfrak q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-localization-radical], $\sqrt{JS_{\mathfrak q}}=\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$. Also $m/1\ne0$ in $P_{\mathfrak q}$: otherwise the zero criterion of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] gives $v\notin\mathfrak q$ with $vm=0$, contradicting $J\subseteq\mathfrak q$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-finite-ring-map-finite], the map $f=\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)$ is finite. Its fibre over $\mathfrak p$ is finite by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. The spectrum convention [def-weil-affine-spectrum] identifies this fibre with the primes of $S$ whose contraction is $\mathfrak p$. Enumerate them without repetition as $\mathfrak q_1=\mathfrak q,\mathfrak q_2,\ldots,\mathfrak q_l$, with $l\ge1$. The map $R\to S$ is integral by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. Hence [pqf-lem-incomparability] shows that these distinct primes are pairwise incomparable.

source.place: Tag 05E1, first proof paragraph; Tag 05DR, lemma-finite-finite-fibres; Tag 00GT, lemma-integral-no-inclusion

proof.text: If $l>1$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] with the ideal $\mathfrak q$ and the prime ideals $\mathfrak q_2,\ldots,\mathfrak q_l$. The noncontainment hypotheses follow from step 2. Obtain $x\in\mathfrak q$ with $x\notin\mathfrak q_i$ for every $i>1$. If $l=1$, take $x=0$; the avoidance condition is empty.

proof.text:
Step 1 gives $(x/1)^t\in JS_{\mathfrak q}$ for some $t\ge1$. Thus $x^tm/1=0$ in $P_{\mathfrak q}$, and [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] gives $y
otin\mathfrak q$ with $yx^tm=0$ in $P$. Put $z=ym$. Since $y$ is invertible in $S_{\mathfrak q}$ and $m/1
e0$, we have $z/1
e0$ in $P_{\mathfrak q}$. For $i>1$, $x$ is invertible in $S_{\mathfrak q_i}$ and $x^tz=0$, so $z/1=0$ in $P_{\mathfrak q_i}$.

Put $T=R\setminus\mathfrak p$, $A=T^{-1}R=R_{\mathfrak p}$, $B=\varphi(T)^{-1}S$ and $N=\varphi(T)^{-1}P$. These fractions and their actions are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. The map $A\to B$ is $r/t\mapsto\varphi(r)/\varphi(t)$, well defined by the fraction relations. If $s_1,\ldots,s_d$ generate $S$ over $R$, they generate $B$ over $A$: $s/\varphi(t)=\sum_j(a_j/t)(s_j/1)$ whenever $s=\sum_j\varphi(a_j)s_j$. Thus $B$ is finite over the local ring $A$, whose maximal ideal is $\mathfrak pA$ by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $B$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-local-radical] gives its contraction $\mathfrak pA$ in $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-spectrum-embedding], its contraction $Q$ in $S$ is prime. For $r\in R$, $\varphi(r)\in Q$ iff $r/1\in\mathfrak pA$ iff $r\in\mathfrak p$ (the last equivalence is the fraction criterion and primality of $\mathfrak p$). Consequently $Q=\mathfrak q_i$ for some $i$.

Fix $r\in\mathfrak p$. By step 1, $(\varphi(r)/1)^k\in JS_{\mathfrak q}$ for some $k\ge1$. Hence $\varphi(r)^kz/1=0$ in $P_{\mathfrak q}$; by step 4 it is also zero in every $P_{\mathfrak q_i}$ for $i>1$. Let $w=\varphi(r)^kz/1\in N$. If $w\ne0$, its annihilator $H=\operatorname{Ann}_B(w)$ is proper. Choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak n\supseteq H$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal]. Step 5 identifies its contraction in $S$ with some $\mathfrak q_i$. Since $\varphi(r)^kz/1=0$ in $P_{\mathfrak q_i}$, [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] gives $u\notin\mathfrak q_i$ with $u\varphi(r)^kz=0$ in $P$. Then $u/1\in H\subseteq\mathfrak n$, contradicting the description of the contraction. Thus $w=0$ in $N$, and the same zero criterion yields $a\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ with $\varphi(a)\varphi(r)^kz=0$. In other words, $ar^k\in\operatorname{Ann}_R(z)$.

source.place: Tag 05E1, second proof paragraph; element detection of Tag 00HN, lemma-characterize-zero-local, written out using an annihilator

proof.text:
Write $I=\operatorname{Ann}_R(z)$. If $b\in I\setminus\mathfrak p$, then $\varphi(b)
otin\mathfrak q$ is invertible in $S_{\mathfrak q}$ and kills $z/1$, contradicting step 4; hence $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Let $\mathfrak p_0\subseteq\mathfrak p$ be a prime containing $I$. For each $r\in\mathfrak p$, step 6 gives $a
otin\mathfrak p$ and $k\ge1$ with $ar^k\in I\subseteq\mathfrak p_0$. As $a
otin\mathfrak p_0$, primality implies $r\in\mathfrak p_0$. Thus $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak p_0$, and equality follows. This proves that $\mathfrak p$ is minimal over the annihilator of the actual element $z\in P$, which is exactly $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_R(P)$.
